answer: Proposed validators salt a 96-GiB memory-hard image per key from a saffron image, a fable text and a whisper recording, then commit its root. Independent auditors challenge every key for unpredictable linked blocks within the same two-second window. A farm can share code or rent RAM, but each clone must reserve another 96 GiB of live memory and read capacity; one image cannot answer different salts on demand. Auditors sign timings; validators deny that key pay on a missing or late proof. This is not a current MinePoA rule.
